content.overview: Article 52 establishes the office of the President of India: there shall be a President of India. The President is the constitutional head of the Union and forms part of Parliament (Article 79).
content.glance: There shall be a President of India — constitutional head of the Union.
content.study:
Article 52:
‘There shall be a President of India.’

This is the constitutive provision for the office. Related provisions govern executive power (Art 53), election (Arts 54–55), term (Art 56), qualifications (Art 58), conditions of office (Art 59), oath (Art 60), impeachment (Art 61), and the Council of Ministers that aids and advises the President (Art 74).

The President is an integral part of Parliament (Art 79) and the formal head of the executive; real executive power is exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers (Art 74, as interpreted in settled jurisprudence including the 42nd and 44th Amendment line).

Examination: state the bare constitutive rule; link to Art 53 (vesting of executive power) and Art 74 (aid and advice).

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. Constitutive provision for the office.
2. President = constitutional head of the Union.
3. Part of Parliament (Art 79).
4. Executive power vested under Art 53; exercised on aid and advice (Art 74).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 52 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 52 provides that there shall be a President of India. It is the constitutive provision for the office of the constitutional head of the Union.

examTips: Art 52 creates the office; Art 53 vests power; Art 74 supplies aid and advice.
